GTK Cyber Data Visualization in Python

GTK Cyber Python Visualization Libraries • Matplotlib: “Lowest” level visualization library. Very powerful, but little abstraction • Pandas/Pyplot: Easier, but requires transformation for complex visualizations • Seaborn: Good for advanced statistical visualizations • Altair: New library: declarative statistical visualization library • Plotly / Cufflinks: Make it interactive!

GTK Cyber Customizing your Charts • Axes: Axes represent an individual plot or chart. • Figure: This is the final complete image and may contain 1 or more axes.

GTK Cyber Customizing your Charts • Matplotlib has both an object-oriented and state- based interface. This can be confusing when you look up answers on Stack Overflow. • Use basic pandas plotting for simple plots • Seaborn, YellowBrick and others for more complex visualizations • Use the OO interface in MatPlotLib to customize simple visualizations.

GTK Cyber Interactive Visualizations

GTK Cyber Interactive Notebooks • There are many modules and tools out there for making Jupyter notebooks interactive. • Ipywidgets, plotly, altair... others.. • Difficult to share w/o a hosted environment. • Poor user experience, not suitable for managers or non-technical users.
GTK Cyber Introducing Streamlit

GTK Cyber Introducing Streamlit • Streamlit is a framework for building interactive, data-driven applications in Python. • Streamlit allows you to quickly and easily create interactive dashboards and applications. • Streamlit abstracts all the javascript and other web components so that a data analyst or data scientist can focus on the data and not web components. • Designed to work with AI.
GTK Cyber You don't run Streamlit in Jupyter

GTK Cyber Starting a Streamlit Application • You must write your code in a standard python file. • When you are ready to launch, simply execute the following command. It will launch a web server to host your application. • From the command line, run: streamlit run your_script.py You will be able to access your application at http://localhost:8501 There are various command line options which you can find in the streamlit docs here: https://docs.streamlit.io/

GTK Cyber Basic Streamlit Concepts import streamlit as st import pandas as pd # Display some text... st.markdown("""# Basic Application This basic application will demonstrate how to display data, both as a table and as a chart.""" ) # Data ingest skipped for brevity # Display the line chart st.area_chart(line_chart_data) st.dataframe(data, hide_index=True)

GTK Cyber Presenting Data with Streamlit • You can see from the previous example how easy it is to present data using Streamlit • Complete charting docs are available here: https://docs.streamlit.io/ develop/api-reference/charts • Each chart can be customized extensively. • Complete code for the basic example is in the streamlit_examples folder in the course github repo.

GTK Cyber Laying Out Your Application • Streamlit has a variety of layout components including tabs, pages, containers, expanders, popovers, modal dialogues and more. • Complete list is available here: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api- reference/layout • You can use the with notation to create a layout option, then add your streamlit elements in that with block

GTK Cyber Laying Out Your Data # Create the tabs chart_tab, table_tab = st.tabs(["Chart", "Data"]) # Display the line chart with chart_tab: st.area_chart(line_chart_data) # Display the table with table_tab: st.dataframe(raw_data, hide_index=True)

GTK Cyber Taking Input from a User • Streamlit has a large collection of input widgets available here: https:// docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/widgets • When the input element is updated, it creates an event which causes the page (and data) to be reloaded. • The code below adds a textbox which will collect a value from the user and display it: • Remember to validate user input! name = st.text_input("Enter your name") if len(name) > 0: st.write(f"Hello, {name}") •

GTK Cyber Building AI Applications with Streamlit • Streamlit has a chat_input and chat_message widget which are built for interacting with LLMs. • Full docs are available here: https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api- reference/chat/st.chat_input
